title: I heard every seat at solar eclipse had a very different experience, ...
transcript: Join me at the theater today I saw a brand new immersive theatrical experience called Solar Eclipse. I actually got up at 4am in the morning to see this. We were given a very specific set of coordinates for this production which I thought was a really cool touch. It was about a four and a half hour drive away in a state park near Syracuse. We had our playbills ready we were prepared but we were kind of nervous because the conditions were not looking great. The backdrop of this production though was stunning. We got to walk around and explore there was an incredible waterfall 10 out of 10 for this. And by the time we were done like things had started to look up a bit. We were getting peaks of the show. We were thinking maybe it could go on. We decided even to move our seats down the road to a little beach, but the closer we got to the actual showtime the more nervous I became because everything was starting to look worse. But we weren’t gonna let it take away from our enjoyment. Every so often we'd be able to see something and it was really cool and special even though it didn't show up on camera. And then when it was time for the big moment. The lights just began to dim. This part was so cool I've been hearing about the totality 11 o clock number but I was unprepared for what it would look like truly went from zero to 100 so quickly just like knowing it was the middle of the day and we were getting this incredible display I was totally in awe. Obviously I wish I'd gotten see a little bit more but it was totally worth the journey and the ride for this moment. And then it was done. This unfortunately is a one night only engagement. Rumor has it they’ll will be a big return in 20 years And you know what I'd go again
